info.title: Product Catalogue API
info.description: A Sanctum-authenticated CRUD API. Issue a token at POST /api/auth/token, then paste it into Swagger UI's Authorize dialog.

post.description: Creates an ordinary account — never an administrator — and returns a Sanctum token for it. Requires an administrator token. The password must be at least 12 characters and contain a letter and a number, and must not appear in known breach data.

201.description: The account was created and a token issued.

422.description: Validation failed, including an email that is already registered.

patch.description: Partial update: any field left out of the body is left unchanged. Changing the password requires `current_password` and revokes all other tokens.

current_password.description: Required, and must match, whenever `password` is present. Ignored otherwise.

422.description: Validation failed, including an email that is already taken or a `current_password` that does not match.

get.description: Display a paginated listing of customers.

post.description: Writes the customer and its profile in one request. Leaving the profile fields out stores the column defaults — a zero credit limit and COD — rather than nulls.

delete.description: Refused with 422 while the customer still has sales.

patch.description: Partial update: any field left out of the body is left unchanged. This endpoint touches the customer's own columns only — use the profile endpoint for the commercial terms.
Creates the profile if the customer does not have one, and amends it if they do.

get.description: Display a paginated listing of products.

delete.description: Also deletes the files behind its gallery.

patch.description: Partial update: any field left out of the body is left unchanged. The gallery follows the same rule — send `images` to replace it, leave it out to keep it, and send an empty list to empty it.

get.description: Display a paginated listing of suppliers.

delete.description: Refused with 422 while the supplier is still paired with products.

patch.description: Partial update: any field left out of the body is left unchanged. Product pairings and their prices are untouched.

post.description: Returns a Sanctum personal access token to be sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

200.description: The issued token and the authenticated user.

delete.description: Revoke the token that authenticated the current request.

id.description:
Also the `Account` component schema. Credentials are deliberately absent:
they are write-only inputs and must never appear in a response.

email_verified_at.description: Always null: this API never sends verification mail.

city_id.description:
Also the `CustomerProfile` component schema: the five columns of
`customer_profiles`.

`city` is a nested object rather than an id, for the same reason the ledger
sends a tag's colour alongside its name — a consumer of this API has no list of
cities to resolve an id against, and an id it cannot resolve is an id it has to
guess about. Omitted when it has not been loaded.

city.description: The city, inlined. Not a $ref to a City schema because this API has no city endpoints and no other resource needs one — a shared schema with a single caller is a second place to change for one line.

id.description:
Also the `Customer` component schema.

The profile is a nested object rather than a flat handful of columns, because it
is a separate row with a lifecycle of its own: a customer exists from the first
order and the profile is written when the desk onboards them. Flattening it would
hide whether `credit_limit` is null because the customer is un-onboarded or
because the value was never set — the same distinction Customer::profile's
comment makes about not defaulting the relation.

Omitted entirely when it has not been loaded, rather than sent as null. An
absent `profile` means "this response did not ask"; a null one would claim the
customer has no profile, which is a statement about the customer.

profile.description: The commercial profile. Absent when the response did not include it; null when the customer has not been onboarded.

id.description: Set when referring to a row the product already has.

path.description: Set for a newly uploaded file. Must already exist on the image disk.

alt_text.description: What the picture shows, for anyone using a screen reader. A blank is stored as null.

sort_order.description: Position in the gallery. Read-only on the way in: the submitted list's order is what becomes the order.

url.description: Where the image can be fetched.

id.description:
Also the `Product` component schema: the same definition backs both the
request bodies and the responses, so `readOnly` fields (id, timestamps) are
hidden by Swagger UI when composing a create or update body.

The gallery is here because the API accepts it on the way in — StoreProductRequest
validates `images` for every caller — so a client could post pictures that were
then dropped without a word. Anything a request may send has to come back out,
or the response is describing a different product than the one that was written.

images.description: The gallery, in gallery order. The first row is the one the catalogue shows as the product's picture.

id.description:
Also the `Supplier` component schema.

`products_count` is here because the supplier table shows it, and a count the
web page can show but the API cannot is a question every consumer has to answer
by writing a paginated query of its own.

products_count.description: Products this supplier is paired with.

bearerAuth.description: Paste the token returned by POST /api/auth/token.
